original_context_note: Compared spec.full_target, spec.hypotheses H001–H006, D001–D007 and P with problem.md:17–48 and the supplied route at lines 52–159. All six original givens remain explicit: both dimension bounds, joint smoothness, the fixed unit q, the pointwise unit constraint, pointwise normal acceleration with an existential real scalar and no scalar regularity, and the common compact support of u−q on every positive closed time interval. Positive integer dimensions are represented by natural dimension indices; under H001 this is the same range of dimensions as the original integer dimensions, not an extra hypothesis or a permission to infer positivity without H001. The approved nontrivial support interpretation, Euclidean/Frobenius normalization, componentwise Laplacian, Lebesgue measure, and exclusion of time zero are retained. D001–D004 are typed derivative aliases, with a disclosed total-derivative convention which agrees with the original derivatives under H002; they grant no analytic properties. D005 preserves exactly the original density, without a factor 1/2. D006 defines its time derivative, whose identity is proved in R002. D007 preserves the original finite integral and is guarded by N002; R002 proves integrability without using E, and R003 and R005 have N002 as a direct input before using E. The source contracts of the nine retained M nodes were compared with their actual successful pinned native probes and relevant source text: M001 inner-product differentiation; M002 countably generated filter dominated convergence; M003 continuous compact-support integrability; M006 derivative-bound mean-value estimate with within derivatives on a closed interval; M007 FTC with complete codomain and interval-integrable derivative; M009 symmetry with its actual minSmoothness threshold; M010 the additive compact continuous bound (not the multiplicative variant); M011 coordinate-extraction measure preservation; M012 symmetric Fubini with S-finite measures. Their full conditions, including structures and measures, appear in the source statements and applications; no external literature theorem is imported from Evans. The graph has one producer for each of N001–N004 and P, and every retained M and N is in P's AND closure. H003 is deliberately retained but unused: the proof uses that q is fixed, not its unit norm. The independent optional explanation at problem.md:62–68 deriving the explicit scalar formula a=|D_xu|²−|u_t|² is omitted: it is not used anywhere in the supplied energy route, and normality alone suffices after tangency. No step in the common-support, dominated-difference-quotient, FTC/Fubini integration-by-parts, or final cancellation route is omitted. I actually read all five own conditional packets; R003 was reread after adding its explicit local indicator χQ. These are same-author closing checks, not independent Audit A or a claim that structural validation certifies the mathematics.

output_notes.note: R001/S001 establishes u·ut=0 from the unit constraint and the derivative of u·u, and S002 establishes ut·(utt−lap)=0 using just the pointwise scalar witness. N001 exports both complete formulas for every spatial point and every positive time, with the derivative aliases defined; R005 needs only the second and does not need a scalar selection or any unexported fact.

R002/S001 exports the actual global density derivative with both factors 2, mixed-partial identification, and smoothness. S002–S004 construct the common compact C and positive enclosing R for each τ>0, explicitly give J,Q and their ranges and box measure, derive vanishing of all positive-order derivatives on the open complement, and prove absolute integrability of every product later integrated. The output contains these formulas and support properties rather than a reference to the producer. It proves integrability at every positive time by τ∈int J, which supplies the independent guard for E. These are exactly the smoothness, joint et continuity, common support, and finite integrability statements consumed by R003, R004 and R005.

R003/S001–S004 prove differentiability of the actual finite E, not a formal integral: a two-sided difference quotient is bounded for all 0<|h|<η by an integrable box indicator, tends pointwise to et, and its integral equals the quotient of E by linearity. The output explicitly states E'(t)=∫et(x,t) dx for every t>0. N002 supplies E's guard and integrability of et, so no limit identity or representation is missing from this port.

R004/S001 gives the displayed derivative of g; S002 makes the coordinate-product integral identification explicit; S003 computes each inner integral by FTC using both zero endpoints and concludes ∫d=0; S004 rearranges the two absolutely integrable summands. N004 exports the exact signed integration-by-parts equality for every positive time and every spatial index, with finiteness of both integrands' absolute integrals. R005 can sum the identities without importing g, I or any private box choice.

R005/S001 uses the four direct N ports to prove all density sections integrable, E differentiable and its derivative zero, retaining the full chain with coefficients 2 and the Laplacian sum. S002 proves constancy on every ordered positive time pair by M006 and covers equal and reversed pairs by equality and symmetry. Thus P contains all three original required conclusions, plus the supplied constancy consequence, on precisely (0,∞) and with no assertion at zero.
